t: A Fon kingdom of the Abomey plateau in present-day Benin, founded in the seventeenth century by a branch of Allada's dynasty.
It became a major supplier of the Atlantic slave trade after conquering the port of Whydah in 1727.
Its women soldiers fought France in 1890–94, but Abomey fell in 1892 and the kingdom was absorbed by 1904.
dyk: Dahomey's women soldiers included a unit of 'reapers' armed with long razors; Europeans called the corps the Amazons, while the Fon called them mino, 'our mothers'.
ev: Houegbadja founds the kingdom and builds the first palace at Abomey
Agaja conquers the Kingdom of Allada
Dahomey conquers Whydah, the leading slave-trading port of the coast
After Oyo invasions, Dahomey becomes a tributary of the Oyo Empire
Ghezo overthrows Adandozan and revives royal power
A Dahomean assault on Abeokuta is repulsed with heavy losses
French troops under Colonel Dodds take Abomey
Behanzin surrenders and is exiled to Martinique
